critiques.title: Use one combined legend so line meaning is not split across two keys
critiques.issue: The trend chart uses both color and stroke pattern to encode bird identity, but it renders separate legends for those channels, forcing readers to reconcile two keys for the same lines.
critiques.rationale: A single combined legend preserves the useful redundant cue while reducing confusion and better supporting readers who cannot rely on color alone.
critiques.evidence: population-trend encodes bird on both color and strokeDash, and both channels define their own legends at the same top-right position.
critiques.suggestion: Keep the dashed-vs-solid distinction on the lines, but hide the extra stroke-dash legend so one legend carries the species labels.

critiques.title: Make the main conservation takeaway explicit in the headline
critiques.issue: The dashboard title names the topic, but it does not state the story's conclusion about common birds declining over time.
critiques.rationale: For a narrative infographic, the headline should carry the main takeaway so readers understand the point before parsing multiple charts.
critiques.evidence: The board title is "Britain's Garden Birds" while the subtitle hints at disappearance, and the charts together show that familiar birds like House Sparrow and Starling remain common but have declined strongly since 1979.
critiques.suggestion: Replace the descriptive title with a takeaway headline that connects present-day familiarity with long-term decline.

critiques.title: Use the same species highlight color across the ranking and callout
critiques.issue: House Sparrow is emphasized with orange in the callout and trend chart, but the ranking chart uses one uniform green for every bar, so the species the story spotlights is not visually carried across views.
critiques.rationale: In a narrative infographic, repeated color is one of the fastest ways to connect the ranked leader, its long-term decline, and the headline fact. The current mismatch weakens that cross-panel linkage.
critiques.evidence: The ranking bars are all colored #5b7a6b, while House Sparrow is colored #d1603d in the trend chart and the did-you-know callout uses the same orange for the −50% figure.
critiques.suggestion: Color the House Sparrow bar with the same orange used elsewhere and keep the remaining bars in a neutral tone.

critiques.title: Use one consistent type system across the board
critiques.issue: The dashboard mixes serif and sans-serif families across the board title, subtitle, and charts, which weakens the infographic's visual coherence.
critiques.rationale: A narrative infographic benefits from a stable editorial voice, and the current type mix makes the board feel assembled from separate parts rather than one story.
critiques.evidence: board typography uses Georgia for the title and system-ui for the subtitle, while the chart specs alternate between Palatino/Georgia and Arial.
critiques.suggestion: Standardize the board and chart typography to BBC Reith so the headline, supporting text, and chart labels read as one designed piece.

critiques.title: Let the index trend use a comparison scale instead of a zero baseline
critiques.issue: The population index line chart forces the y-scale to start at zero even though all values sit between about 42 and 124, compressing the visible separation between recovering and declining species.
critiques.rationale: For an indexed time-series whose purpose is to compare relative change from a common baseline of 100, a zero baseline is not required and makes the key divergence harder to see in this small narrative panel.
critiques.evidence: The y encoding uses scale.zero true, while the plotted index values range from 42 to 124 and the chart's story is about long-term change since 1979.
critiques.suggestion: Set the y-scale to the observed comparison range so the decline of House Sparrow and Starling versus the stability of Blue Tit reads more clearly.

critiques.title: Include the final year on the trend axis
critiques.issue: The trend line extends to 2023, but the x-axis labels stop at 2020, making the endpoint year less explicit.
critiques.rationale: Because the story hinges on long-term change through the latest observation, the axis should label the final year readers are being asked to interpret.
critiques.evidence: The data includes 2023 values for all three birds, but the x-axis values list only 1979, 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020.
critiques.suggestion: Add 2023 to the x-axis tick values so the latest endpoint is clearly marked.

critiques.title: Remove exploratory prompts that do not fit the infographic reading mode
critiques.issue: The dashboard includes click-to-focus instructions and selection mechanics inside a narrative infographic, even though the story is meant to be read as a fixed explanation rather than explored as an analysis tool.
critiques.rationale: These prompts add interface language and dimming behavior that compete with the editorial reading flow without being necessary to understand the story.
critiques.evidence: The bird filter panel is visible, the ranking tile subtitle text mentions clicking a bird to spotlight it, the trend subtitle mentions clicking a legend name to focus, and both charts include selection-driven opacity changes.
critiques.suggestion: Remove the click-selection behavior from both linked charts and delete the click-to-focus instruction text so the infographic reads as a fixed narrative while preserving the static encodings.
